proposals.before: Clan and marriage various divisions assembling for the funeral exceeded ten thousand; Mengxun wept and said to the masses: "Formerly when Han's mandate was mid-faint, my great-grandfather aided and encouraged Dou Rong, preserving and quieting the west of the River.

proposals.before: Mengxun remonstrated saying: "Returning hosts do not block; exhausted bandits are not pursued—this is the military family's rong.
proposals.after: Mengxun remonstrated saying: "Returning hosts do not block; exhausted bandits are not pursued—this is the military specialists' precept.
proposals.reason: The source idiom is the soldiers' precept (兵家之戒); rendering 戎 as rong leaves the sentence meaningless.

proposals.before: Ye relied on Mengxun to escape, sighed saying: "I alone could not use Zifang's words, thereby reaching to this!"
proposals.after: Ye relied on Mengxun to escape, sighed saying: "I could not use Zifang's words, thereby reaching to this!"

proposals.before: Mengxun feared Ye could not contain himself, always hiding wisdom to avoid him.
proposals.after: Mengxun feared Ye could not tolerate him, always hiding wisdom to avoid him.

proposals.before: Ma Quan, a gentleman attendant at Duan Ye's gate, was dashing and brilliant, with military talent above the common run.

proposals.before: Ye's gatehouse gentleman Ma Quan was handsome and bright with transcendent qi, martial plans surpassing others.
proposals.after: Ye's Menxia shilang Ma Quan was handsome and bright with transcendent qi, martial plans surpassing others.

proposals.after: Mengxun reached Zhangye; Ang's elder brother's son Cheng'ai cut open the gate and admitted him; Ye's left and right all scattered.

proposals.before: Mengxun's paternal uncles, Central-Field Protector Qinxin and Linsong governor Kong Du, together were arrogant and wasteful, encroaching and harming; the hundred surnames suffered them.
proposals.after: Mengxun's paternal uncles, Central-Field Protector Qinxin and Linsong governor Kongdu, together were arrogant and wasteful, encroaching and harming; the hundred surnames suffered them.
proposals.reason: 孔篤 is the personal name of Mengxun's paternal uncle (伯父), parallel to 親信; as a 伯父 he is a Juqu, so 'Kong Du' wrongly presents 孔 as a surname. Romanize the given name as Kongdu.

proposals.after: Mengxun's uncles Qinxin, warden of the central fields, and Kongdu, governor of Linsong, were arrogant predators, and the people groaned under them.

proposals.before: Mengxun raided Di Luoquan at Fanhe, did not overcome him, moved more than five hundred households and returned.
proposals.after: Mengxun raided Di Luopan at Fanhe, did not overcome him, moved more than five hundred households and returned.
proposals.reason: 磐 in 狄洛磐 is pán (as in 熾磐 Chipan in this chapter); 'Luoquan' does not match the characters. The extraction's own pinyin is Dí Luòpán.

proposals.before: Mengxun struck Di Luoquan at Fanhe, failed to take him, and carried off over five hundred households on the retreat.
proposals.after: Mengxun struck Di Luopan at Fanhe, failed to take him, and carried off over five hundred households on the retreat.
proposals.reason: 狄洛磐 is Di Luopan (磐 pán); 'Luoquan' misreads the last character.

proposals.before: Nutan's Huanghe governor Wen Zhi held the Huangchuan; guard commander Marquis Cheng Yi led the host to submit.
proposals.after: Nutan's Huanghe governor Wenzhi held the Huangchuan; guard commander Cheng Yihou led the host to submit.
proposals.reason: 文支 is Nutan's younger brother (僉檀弟文支, s0162), i.e. a Tufa, so 'Wen Zhi' wrongly presents 文 as a surname. 成宜侯 is repeated as a bare name in the appointment list of s0156 (成宜侯為振威將軍), so it reads as a personal name, not 'Marquis Cheng Yi'; no marquisate is stated.

proposals.before: Wen Zhi, Nutan's governor on the Huang River, held the Huangchuan, while Cheng Yi, guard commander, brought his command over to Mengxun.
proposals.after: Wenzhi, Nutan's governor on the Huang River, held the Huangchuan, while Cheng Yihou, guard commander, brought his command over to Mengxun.
proposals.reason: 文支 is Nutan's brother (s0162), so Wenzhi is a given name, not surname Wen; 成宜侯 recurs as a bare name in s0156 and should be romanized in full rather than truncated to 'Cheng Yi'.

proposals.before: He appointed Wen Zhi grand general who guards the east, governor of Guangwu, marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yi as general who rouses might, governor of Huangchuan; and palace general Wang Jian as Huanghe governor.
proposals.after: He appointed Wenzhi grand general who guards the east, governor of Guangwu, marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yihou as general who rouses might, governor of Huangchuan; and palace general Wang Jian as Huanghe governor.
proposals.reason: Same persons as s0155: 文支 is Nutan's brother Wenzhi (not surname Wen); 成宜侯 is named in full as the appointee (成宜侯為振威將軍), so 'Cheng Yi' drops part of the name.

proposals.before: He named Wen Zhi grand general of the east, governor of Guangwu, and marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yi general who rouses might and governor of Huangchuan; and Wang Jian of the palace guard as governor of the Huang River.
proposals.after: He named Wenzhi grand general of the east, governor of Guangwu, and marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yihou general who rouses might and governor of Huangchuan; and Wang Jian of the palace guard as governor of the Huang River.
proposals.reason: Repeated names from s0155: Wenzhi (Nutan's brother, s0162) and the full name 成宜侯 Cheng Yihou.

proposals.after: Nutan's younger brother Wenzhi, tracing Xiang Bo's meaning in returning to Han, holds that heavy screen and requests to be minister and concubine.

proposals.before: Gou replied saying: "Nutan is light, crafty, and not benevolent; sincere good faith not yet manifest—the sagely court therefore added his heavy noble is to praise his returning to good and immediate ordering's meaning only.
proposals.after: Gou replied saying: "Nutan is light, crafty, and not benevolent; his sincere good faith is not yet manifest—that the sagely court added his heavy noble rank was only to praise the principle that one who returns to good is at once given place.
proposals.reason: 聖朝所以加其重爵者，褒其歸善即敘之義耳: the literal dropped 爵 (rank) and inserted a meaningless 'is'; 所以…者…耳 is 'the reason that… was only to…', and 歸善即敘 is 'returning to good and being promptly ranked'.

proposals.before: Mengxun offered sacrifice west of Jin Mountain and sent Juqu Guangzong with ten thousand cavalry against the Wuti tribes, winning a great victory.
proposals.after: Mengxun went west to sacrifice at Jin Mountain and sent Juqu Guangzong with ten thousand cavalry against the Wuti tribes, winning a great victory.
proposals.reason: 蒙遜西祀金山: 西 is the direction of travel and the sacrifice is at Jin Mountain (the literal already reads 'sacrificed west at Jin Mountain'); 'west of Jin Mountain' mislocates it.

proposals.before: Ye feared Mengxun's heroic martialness, slightly wished to distance him; thereupon made Mengxun's paternal uncle Yisheng Jiuquan governor, Mengxun Linchi governor.
proposals.after: Ye feared Mengxun's heroic martialness, slightly wished to distance him; thereupon made Mengxun's paternal cousin-uncle (his father's cousin) Yisheng Jiuquan governor, Mengxun Linchi governor.
proposals.reason: 從叔益生: 從叔 is the father's younger paternal cousin, not a 叔父; 'paternal uncle' loses the 從 degree (cf. accepted 從祖 repair r0017/r0020).

proposals.before: He issued a writ saying: "I hope to rely on the ancestral temple's spirit, Heaven and Earth's blessing, to ford the not-yet-stripped turning, save the surviving black-haired from bitter herbs, above hope to sweep clear foul qi, below hope to protect and quiet household blessing.
proposals.after: He issued a writ saying: "I hope to rely on the ancestral temple's spirit, Heaven and Earth's blessing, to ford the turning of Obstruction and Stripping (adversity), save the surviving black-haired from bitter herbs, above hope to sweep clear foul qi, below hope to protect and quiet household blessing.
proposals.reason: 濟否剝之運會: 否 and 剝 are the hexagrams Pi (Obstruction) and Bo (Stripping), a figure for adversity; reading 否 as a negation ('not-yet-stripped') is wrong.

proposals.before: Inwardly examining all bodies, I do not know where crime lies.
proposals.after: Inwardly examining myself, I do not know where the crime lies.
proposals.reason: 內省諸身: 諸 = 之於 ('examine it in oneself', cf. 吾日三省吾身), not 'all'; 'all bodies' misreads it.

proposals.before: Jiao Chang and Duan Jing secretly invited Chipan in; Chipan advanced again against Hanping.
proposals.after: Hanping's chief clerk Jiao Chang and the general Duan Jing secretly sent letters inviting Chipan in, and Chipan advanced again against Hanping.
proposals.reason: 漢平長史焦昶、將軍段景密信招熾磐: the idiomatic dropped that Jiao Chang was Hanping's 長史 and Duan Jing a 將軍, and the 密信 (secret letters); restore them (literal already has them).
